cars.variant: Rallye 2 — original Chrysler France road brochure
cars.specification_market: Original Chrysler France brochure scans, including physical pages 3–4 and technical back page, were read. The leaflet is undated; 1972 is programme-introduction context from Caramulo, not a certified print date or pictured car year. Native CH DIN is retained. No Rallye 1, Rallye 3, later tune or competition conversion is imported. The museum’s 86-cv specification concerns a subsequently prepared racer and is excluded. One 1000 Rallye road family is counted.
cars.summary: The Rallye 2 turned the rear-engined Simca into a defining small-capacity club-motorsport car. Its factory road offering combines a twin-carburettor engine, strengthened suspension and four disc brakes, while the Caramulo collection documents its successful competition use.

cars.variant: Active Top — June 2002 Japan five-speed manual launch reference
cars.specification_market: Daihatsu’s 19 June 2002 Japanese launch release. Select the five-speed Active Top road car. The four-cylinder/16-valve engine establishes four valves per cylinder. Displacement is not specified in this release and is not guessed. The later detachable roof, optional Sports Pack, Ultimate trim, 1.3-litre export engine and second-generation D-Frame are excluded. The first-kei powered-roof statement is dated June 2002; no current production claim is made.
cars.summary: The original Copen is a landmark kei roadster, pairing a dedicated turbocharged sporting chassis with the class’s first powered folding hardtop as of June 2002. Its lasting following and role as Daihatsu’s sporting flagship establish significance beyond anniversary-edition rarity.
cars.admission_reason: The original Copen is a landmark kei roadster, pairing a dedicated turbocharged sporting chassis with the class’s first powered folding hardtop as of June 2002. Its lasting following and role as Daihatsu’s sporting flagship establish significance beyond anniversary-edition rarity.

cars.variant: 135 M — 1939 Museo Nicolis Chapron cabriolet reference
cars.specification_market: Custodian’s own 1939 135 M road cabriolet. Quoted power and speed remain catalogue claims. Its displacement field is blank and dimension units are implausible; those fields are omitted. The Cotal is described by its mechanism, without calling it a modern automatic. No racing 135 S/CS tune, MS engine, celebrity history or untouched condition is inferred. One 135 family is counted.
cars.summary: The 135 established Delahaye’s international sporting reputation through related touring and racing versions. The selected fast-road Chapron cabriolet represents the family’s road-going grand-touring identity, including its distinctive electromagnetic transmission and convertible coachwork.
